turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You put a zero on Owen's essay before anyone called me. Explain that.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero rests on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. People draft in one place and paste into another, so a paste proves where it landed, not who wrote it. And before you entered anything, did anyone ask Owen?
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every week, Hale. A wrong line is a mistake, not a verdict. Was Owen heard before that zero, yes or no?

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.

I never said December 1 in this room, but you have it right. To put this behind him, he'll do your rewrite this Thursday, private, in your room, with the mark in by Monday and nothing on his record. Tonight's email says all of that, plus your apology for entering the zero first, and it goes to the principal too.
He'll be there Thursday. Send the email.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite in your room this Thursday, that you will mark it by Monday so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and that nothing will be placed in his record. I still require all of this in writing, along with your apology for entering the zero before contacting me. I expect that written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, marked by Monday, with nothing on his record; she still wants it confirmed in writing tonight with your apology, copied to the principal, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and answered her pasting defence by offering to examine any earlier file's dates together, which gave her something she could check.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, though she asked three times, and you said she had raised December 1 when she hadn't; both gave her procedure to fight on.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay's work between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after showing the version history, when she asked whether anyone spoke to Owen first, answer that directly before moving to your second piece of evidence.
